binding_record_note: Four public native function templates join to four real Rust constructor-callback methods. The protected emplaceImpl template joins separately to its compiler-emitted shared private engine specialization; this does not claim a direct generic Rust protected-template surface or add global completion credit.
changes: Added emplace_with, emplaced_with, try_emplace_with and try_emplaced_with. Each accepts a deferred FnOnce key constructor and requires only the existing HashPolicy bound, preserving support for non-Debug, non-Clone and non-Default keys and policies.

Split insertion preparation from prepared placement so native ReSize runs before construction exactly once. Existing consuming and mixed-ownership insertion methods share the same prepared lookup/replacement/allocation body.

Empty constructor failure retains the newly allocated bucket table with zero nodes; growth constructor failure retains the completed 101-to-1009 rehash and original node addresses/order. Native rehash callback order precedes the key-conversion event.

All four methods construct a temporary before duplicate lookup, including Try variants. An unused duplicate Try temporary is destroyed before return, while the existing tagged key remains unchanged in its original node.

Tracked noncopyable keys prove no key destructor runs when construction itself throws, and a completed temporary is destroyed during hash/equality failure before the exception reaches the caller. Tagged temporary and stored payloads distinguish their destruction and retention.

Direct native integer-key conversion probes cover empty insertion, existing/new keys, constructor/hash/equality failures and growth for each return/try variant. Node counts, bucket allocation/count, allocator active allocations, first-node identity and full insertion order match.
The existing K-taking methods remain available with their consuming Rust transfer behavior. The new callback methods add the previously missing deferred-construction domain.

Updated from integrated main containing the prior ordered constructor-lifetime and protected-lookup batches. The sole additive module declaration conflict retained all three contributions, followed by combined validation.
limitations: This scoped constructor-phase port does not establish class-wide or global API/test parity.

Successful key transfer uses Rust moves. Arbitrary C++ user-defined key move constructors and destructors of moved-from temporaries are not implicitly reproduced; successful-transfer native probes use int keys with traced converting arguments.

Tracked nontrivial-key probes deliberately cover paths without key transfer: duplicate Try hits, constructor failure and hash/equality failure. They do not certify replacement or insertion involving custom C++ key move callbacks.

Rust constructor closures adapt native variadic forwarding. Arbitrary C++ argument-pack evaluation, owned argument temporary destruction, conversions and throwing move policies still require separately specified policies.

C++ noexcept termination differs from Rust panic propagation. Native probes use potentially throwing constructors/hash/equality callbacks and ordinary nonthrowing tracked destructors; double-panic and allocation-failure termination domains are not certified.

Existing ReSize panic rollback remains distinct from native partial bucket rewiring when a hasher throws during rehash. This batch proves completed rehash before a later constructor failure, not that unresolved failing-rehash domain.
The protected emplaceImpl record binds the shared Rust implementation specialization, not a direct public generic equivalent of both native compile-time return selectors.
Safe detached cursor ownership checks, non-owning registry overhead, raw bucket mutation contracts and safe set FirstNode unit views remain separately tracked adaptations.
Scoped native/compiler/Miri evidence does not replace whole-workspace validation or inventory completeness proof.
compiler_warning_note: Nightly rustdoc warnings outside this Emplace scope are retained in raw output; scoped Clippy is run with warnings denied.
